questions.title: How do you maintain human oversight of AI-driven development?
questions.description: Assess ownership, plan review, approval boundaries, clarification, and renewed validation when scope changes.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Assign accountable human reviewers

helpfulResource.displayText: Named reviewers own business, architecture, implementation, and release decisions. Evidence includes a responsibility matrix and review records.

improvementPlan.displayText: Assign accountable owners for each decision category and publish their review responsibilities and escalation paths.

choices.title: Review AI-generated plans before execution

helpfulResource.displayText: A human checks proposed scope, assumptions, risks, and execution steps before the agent proceeds. Evidence includes an approved plan revision.

improvementPlan.displayText: Add a plan review checkpoint and require explicit approval of the proposed actions before executing the plan.

choices.title: Define approval boundaries for consequential actions

helpfulResource.displayText: Production changes, destructive operations, and privileged actions have explicit authorization boundaries. Evidence includes tool policies and approval records.

improvementPlan.displayText: Classify consequential actions, configure tool restrictions, and require an authorized reviewer before those actions occur.

choices.title: Clarify ambiguous requirements before implementation

helpfulResource.displayText: The agent surfaces unresolved requirements and assumptions rather than silently making material business decisions. Evidence includes answered clarification questions.

improvementPlan.displayText: Record ambiguities and obtain product or engineering decisions before implementing the affected behavior.

choices.title: Revalidate approvals after material scope changes

helpfulResource.displayText: An approval remains associated with the scope and artifact revision reviewed. Material changes trigger renewed review.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define material-change criteria and reopen approval when scope, risk, or architecture changes beyond the approved plan.

questions.title: Testing: Is AI test generation integrated into the development workflow, and how are outputs validated?
questions.description: Assess AI-assisted test creation, review, version control, automated execution, and independent validation of generated software.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Validate outputs against approved acceptance criteria

helpfulResource.displayText: Acceptance criteria are established before implementation and checked against actual results. Evidence includes reviewed criteria and acceptance results.

improvementPlan.displayText: Create measurable acceptance criteria for each story and document whether the implementation satisfies each criterion.

choices.title: Independently review generated code

helpfulResource.displayText: Human review checks business logic, architectural fit, error handling, and unsupported assumptions before merge.

improvementPlan.displayText: Require a qualified reviewer to inspect generated changes and resolve material findings before merge.

choices.title: Review generated tests for completeness

helpfulResource.displayText: Reviewers inspect test expectations and edge cases so generated tests do not simply reproduce implementation mistakes.

improvementPlan.displayText: Compare tests with approved requirements. Add missing negative, boundary, and failure-path cases before acceptance.

choices.title: Run functional and integration tests

helpfulResource.displayText: Automated tests exercise expected behavior and interactions with dependencies. Evidence includes execution reports tied to a source revision.

improvementPlan.displayText: Add unit, integration, and acceptance checks appropriate to the change and block release on required failures.

choices.title: Perform security and dependency checks

helpfulResource.displayText: Security checks examine code, dependencies, and exposed credentials. Findings are triaged against the release policy.

improvementPlan.displayText: Integrate code, dependency, and secret scanning into the delivery pipeline and remediate release-blocking findings.

choices.title: Validate applicable non-functional requirements

helpfulResource.displayText: Performance, resilience, accessibility, and other applicable requirements have measurable thresholds and validation evidence.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define relevant non-functional thresholds, execute representative tests, and address failures before production release.

choices.title: Integrate AI test generation into the development workflow

helpfulResource.displayText: The workflow includes AI-assisted creation or extension of tests for applicable changes, with traceability to acceptance criteria and independent review of expected results.

improvementPlan.displayText: Add an explicit AI test-generation step for applicable changes and review generated assertions against requirements before accepting the tests.

choices.title: Maintain and execute generated tests with the codebase

helpfulResource.displayText: Accepted generated tests are version-controlled, run in the applicable local or CI workflow, and updated when intended behavior changes.

improvementPlan.displayText: Commit reviewed generated tests alongside the implementation and include them in required automated verification.

questions.title: How do you protect sensitive information and constrain AI tool access?
questions.description: Assess proposed enterprise security controls for development agents. These controls extend the AI-DLC methodology and must be tailored to the selected tools.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Restrict agent permissions to approved tasks

helpfulResource.displayText: Agent identities have only the repository, environment, and tool access required for their current responsibilities. Evidence includes reviewed permissions.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use scoped roles and temporary credentials. Remove unnecessary access and review permissions when task responsibilities change.

choices.title: Control sensitive information in AI context

helpfulResource.displayText: The team defines which source code and data may enter each approved AI environment and checks inputs and retained artifacts for sensitive content.

improvementPlan.displayText: Document permitted data classifications, configure tool-specific data controls, and redact information that is not authorized for the selected environment.

choices.title: Keep credentials out of prompts and repositories

helpfulResource.displayText: Secrets are obtained through approved credential mechanisms instead of being embedded in instructions, source files, or retained transcripts.

improvementPlan.displayText: Move secrets to an approved secrets manager, use temporary credentials where supported, scan artifacts, and rotate exposed credentials.

choices.title: Isolate execution and review external instructions

helpfulResource.displayText: Development execution is separated from production, and external repository or tool content is treated as untrusted input. Evidence includes environment boundaries and tool policies.

improvementPlan.displayText: Run agents in restricted development environments and require review before external instructions can authorize privileged or destructive actions.

questions.title: Artifacts: Are technical documents reviewed by AI before human review?
questions.description: Assess an explicit AI-first review sequence for applicable technical documents while retaining accountable human validation.

helpfulResource.displayText: Custom assessment practices added to cover the requested team-adoption topics. The reference supports related AI-DLC principles. It does not prescribe every practice below. Select all implemented practices supported by evidence. Document justified non-applicability where a capability is outside the team s scope.

choices.title: Run an AI review before human document review

helpfulResource.displayText: Applicable design documents, technical specifications, and runbooks receive an AI review for completeness, contradictions, and standards alignment before the human review begins.

improvementPlan.displayText: Add an AI pre-review step for applicable document types and provide the agent with the approved requirements and review checklist.

choices.title: Resolve or disposition AI findings before human approval

helpfulResource.displayText: Authors record how material AI findings were corrected or rejected, and human reviewers validate the document and its unresolved concerns. AI review does not replace human approval.

improvementPlan.displayText: Include the AI review summary and finding dispositions with the human review request, then record the responsible reviewer s decision.

questions.title: Autonomy: Do agents initiate work without a new human prompt within a defined semi-autonomous scope?
questions.description: Assess event- or schedule-triggered initiation under standing authorization, with explicit limits, observability, and escalation. Broad autonomy is not required for every workload.

helpfulResource.displayText: Custom assessment practices added to cover the requested team-adoption topics. The reference supports related AI-DLC principles. It does not prescribe every practice below. Select all implemented practices supported by evidence. Document justified non-applicability where a capability is outside the team s scope.

choices.title: Define the permitted level and scope of autonomy

helpfulResource.displayText: The team documents whether agents are prompt-driven, event-triggered, or scheduled, which work may begin under standing authorization, and which decisions remain human-controlled.

improvementPlan.displayText: Document permitted triggers, task boundaries, permissions, and approval requirements before enabling semi-autonomous execution.

choices.title: Enable approved event- or schedule-triggered initiation

helpfulResource.displayText: For suitable use cases, an approved event or schedule starts a bounded task without a fresh human prompt. Evidence includes trigger configuration and execution records.

improvementPlan.displayText: Select a suitable bounded use case, approve its trigger and execution scope, and verify that initiation works without additional prompting.

choices.title: Apply stop conditions and escalate uncertain decisions

helpfulResource.displayText: Initiated work has time, usage, retry, and action limits. Agents stop or escalate when scope, confidence, or authorization becomes insufficient.

improvementPlan.displayText: Configure execution limits and escalation paths and verify that agents stop before exceeding standing authorization.

choices.title: Record and review autonomous runs

helpfulResource.displayText: Each triggered run records its initiating event, actions, outputs, and approvals so owners can inspect behavior and disable ineffective automation.

improvementPlan.displayText: Retain run records, review representative outcomes, and provide an owner-controlled mechanism to pause or disable triggers.

questions.title: How do you maintain traceability from business intent to production?
questions.description: Assess bidirectional links between intent, requirements, design, implementation, verification, and deployed releases.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Assign stable identifiers to lifecycle artifacts

helpfulResource.displayText: Intents, requirements, Units, and tests have stable identifiers that support durable cross-references.

improvementPlan.displayText: Introduce a consistent identifier scheme and apply it to new and materially changed lifecycle artifacts.

choices.title: Link requirements to implementation and verification

helpfulResource.displayText: A reviewer can trace a requirement to design decisions, source changes, and test evidence, and navigate those links in reverse.

improvementPlan.displayText: Add requirement references to designs, pull requests, and tests. Review and resolve gaps before acceptance.

choices.title: Link releases to approved source revisions

helpfulResource.displayText: Release records identify the source commit, build, configuration, and artifact deployed into each environment.

improvementPlan.displayText: Record source and build identifiers in the release process and retain the relationship between approvals and deployment artifacts.

questions.title: How do you record AI interactions and human decisions?
questions.description: Assess retained evidence of material instructions, approvals, configuration, and unresolved or overridden recommendations.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Retain material AI instructions and outputs

helpfulResource.displayText: Task instructions, context references, and consequential outputs are retained with sensitive information redacted.

improvementPlan.displayText: Configure an approved interaction-recording process and retain the information needed to reconstruct material development decisions.

choices.title: Record approvals, rejections, and overrides

helpfulResource.displayText: Decision records identify the reviewer, time, outcome, rationale, and exact artifact revision reviewed.

improvementPlan.displayText: Introduce a decision record linked to each material approval or override and require renewed review when relevant changes invalidate it.

choices.title: Record relevant model and tool configuration

helpfulResource.displayText: Available model identifiers, agent versions, workflow rules, and relevant tool settings are recorded for investigation. Identical output is not assumed.

improvementPlan.displayText: Capture supported configuration metadata with each delivery run and record changes that may affect generated results.

choices.title: Track open risks and their disposition

helpfulResource.displayText: Material risks and unresolved recommendations have an owner and a recorded resolution or authorized acceptance.

improvementPlan.displayText: Maintain a risk register linked to affected work. Require documented treatment or acceptance before crossing the relevant release gate.

questions.title: How do you preserve verifiable evidence of testing and deployment?
questions.description: Assess completeness, attribution, retention, and protection of verification and release evidence.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Retain test and security validation reports

helpfulResource.displayText: Reports identify the tested build, execution time, outcome, findings, and relevant exceptions.

improvementPlan.displayText: Store verification reports with build identifiers and require retrievable evidence for all mandatory release checks.

choices.title: Preserve deployment and rollback records

helpfulResource.displayText: Records show what changed, where it was deployed, who authorized it, and the outcome of deployment or rollback.

improvementPlan.displayText: Capture release approvals, environment changes, deployment results, and rollback events in a retained release history.

choices.title: Define evidence retention and access controls

helpfulResource.displayText: Retention periods and authorized access reflect organizational obligations. Evidence is protected from unauthorized alteration.

improvementPlan.displayText: Assign evidence owners, configure retention and access policies, and review whether stored records remain complete and retrievable.

questions.title: How do you structure work for parallel AI-driven delivery?
questions.description: Assess how Units, integration boundaries, and Bolts enable coordinated incremental delivery across teams.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Decompose intents into cohesive, loosely coupled Units

helpfulResource.displayText: Each Unit has a clear purpose and scope, while dependencies are limited enough to allow independent progress.

improvementPlan.displayText: Review the decomposition with business and technical owners. Split tightly coupled work and define acceptance criteria for each Unit.

choices.title: Define integration contracts before parallel implementation

helpfulResource.displayText: Teams agree on API, event, and schema expectations before dependent implementations diverge.

improvementPlan.displayText: Document integration contracts and compatibility expectations, then validate them with appropriate contract or integration tests.

choices.title: Deliver through small, verifiable Bolts

helpfulResource.displayText: Each Bolt delivers a bounded increment with explicit validation and integration checkpoints.

improvementPlan.displayText: Reduce oversized increments and plan short build-validation cycles with clear completion evidence.

questions.title: How do you manage context across teams and development sessions?
questions.description: Assess persistent context, selective retrieval, session handoff, and freshness of shared artifacts.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Persist approved context in shared repositories

helpfulResource.displayText: Requirements, designs, decisions, and progress remain accessible to authorized teams and agents across sessions.

improvementPlan.displayText: Store authoritative artifacts in version-controlled locations and define ownership and access for each context category.

choices.title: Load task-relevant context selectively

helpfulResource.displayText: Agents receive relevant current instructions and artifacts without indiscriminately loading every project document.

improvementPlan.displayText: Organize context by project, Unit, and task. Use supported selective-loading mechanisms and review conflicting instructions.

choices.title: Define session handoff and context refresh procedures

helpfulResource.displayText: A resumed session can identify completed work, open decisions, current revisions, and next actions.

improvementPlan.displayText: Save a handoff record and check authoritative artifact revisions before resuming work or transferring it to another team.

questions.title: How do you scale delivery capacity while maintaining quality and cost control?
questions.description: Assess automation, usage controls, review throughput, and balanced delivery outcomes as adoption expands.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Automate repeatable build and verification tasks

helpfulResource.displayText: CI/CD performs repeatable checks consistently so increased generation volume does not bypass required verification.

improvementPlan.displayText: Integrate build, test, and policy checks into CI/CD and remove manual steps that do not require judgment.

choices.title: Manage agent concurrency, usage, and expenditure

helpfulResource.displayText: Tool usage, concurrent work, retries, and expenditure have owners and defined operating limits.

improvementPlan.displayText: Set tool-specific concurrency and spending controls, monitor usage, and define responses to throttling or abnormal consumption.

choices.title: Measure delivery outcomes alongside quality

helpfulResource.displayText: Lead time and delivery volume are assessed alongside defects, failed changes, recovery, and cost.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish a baseline and review lead time, change failures, escaped defects, recovery time, and cost per accepted change together.

choices.title: Scale review and integration capacity with generated work

helpfulResource.displayText: Review queues and integration failures are monitored so AI-generated output does not exceed the team s validation capacity.

improvementPlan.displayText: Track review backlog and integration delays. Limit work in progress and add qualified review capacity where bottlenecks persist.

questions.title: Plan & Define: Are AI tools involved in product definition or backlog management?
questions.description: Assess actual AI participation in product discovery, requirements elaboration, and backlog refinement, with product ownership retained by humans.

helpfulResource.displayText: Custom assessment practices added to cover the requested team-adoption topics. The reference supports related AI-DLC principles. It does not prescribe every practice below. Select all implemented practices supported by evidence. Document justified non-applicability where a capability is outside the team s scope.

choices.title: Use AI to elaborate product intent and requirements

helpfulResource.displayText: AI helps turn a product goal into requirement drafts, clarification questions, and proposed acceptance criteria. Evidence includes AI-assisted definition artifacts reviewed by the product owner.

improvementPlan.displayText: Introduce AI-assisted requirements elaboration for suitable product work and have the product owner validate business intent and acceptance criteria.

choices.title: Use AI during backlog refinement

helpfulResource.displayText: AI assists with story decomposition, missing-detail identification, dependency analysis, or suggested backlog updates. Humans own priority and commitment decisions.

improvementPlan.displayText: Add AI assistance to backlog refinement and validate suggested stories, dependencies, and priorities before updating the authoritative backlog.

choices.title: Link approved planning outputs to tracked work

helpfulResource.displayText: Accepted AI planning outputs become linked backlog items with owners and acceptance criteria rather than remaining only in chat.

improvementPlan.displayText: Connect reviewed AI planning artifacts to the team s backlog and retain the relationship to the originating product intent.

questions.title: Pipelines: Is your pipeline full CI/CD, and do agents triage or resolve pipeline failures?
questions.description: Assess integration-to-deployment automation, distinguish continuous delivery from continuous deployment, and evaluate agent-assisted diagnosis and bounded remediation.

helpfulResource.displayText: Custom assessment practices added to cover the requested team-adoption topics. The reference supports related AI-DLC principles. It does not prescribe every practice below. Select all implemented practices supported by evidence. Document justified non-applicability where a capability is outside the team s scope.

choices.title: Automate continuous integration and validation

helpfulResource.displayText: Relevant source changes trigger repeatable builds, automated tests, and required quality checks. Pipeline results are linked to the tested source revision.

improvementPlan.displayText: Configure source-triggered build and validation stages and prevent required failed checks from being bypassed.

choices.title: Automate the deployment path and declare release gates

helpfulResource.displayText: A repeatable pipeline promotes versioned artifacts through applicable environments. The team records whether production release uses manual approval or automatic deployment and why.

improvementPlan.displayText: Automate artifact promotion and deployment, document the chosen delivery or deployment model, and retain required production authorization and rollback controls.

choices.title: Use agents to triage pipeline failures

helpfulResource.displayText: Agents examine failed stages, logs, test results, and recent changes and propose evidence-backed causes to the responsible developer.

improvementPlan.displayText: Connect an approved agent to relevant pipeline evidence and have developers validate its diagnosis before accepting a proposed fix.

choices.title: Validate agent-proposed pipeline remediation

helpfulResource.displayText: Agents propose or apply fixes within authorized scope. Corrected builds and tests rerun, and consequential changes follow the approval policy.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define permitted remediation actions, create a reviewed fix workflow, and require successful revalidation before promotion.

questions.title: Operations: Do agents assist with on-call triage or incident investigation?
questions.description: Assess agent access to relevant operational context, evidence-backed incident investigation, and controlled execution of approved mitigations.

helpfulResource.displayText: Custom assessment practices added to cover the requested team-adoption topics. The reference supports related AI-DLC principles. It does not prescribe every practice below. Select all implemented practices supported by evidence. Document justified non-applicability where a capability is outside the team s scope.

choices.title: Use agents to summarize and triage operational alerts

helpfulResource.displayText: An approved agent helps the on-call responder correlate alerts with relevant metrics, logs, traces, and recent releases while preserving responder accountability.

improvementPlan.displayText: Provide scoped access to operational telemetry and deployment context and introduce agent-generated triage summaries into the on-call workflow.

choices.title: Ground incident investigation in verifiable evidence

helpfulResource.displayText: Agent findings cite relevant observations and distinguish confirmed facts from hypotheses. Responders validate conclusions and retain investigation records.

improvementPlan.displayText: Require evidence references in agent investigations and have responders verify proposed causes and document confirmed findings.

choices.title: Constrain operational mitigation to approved runbooks

helpfulResource.displayText: Agent-suggested mitigations follow validated runbooks and authorization boundaries. Production actions and outcomes are recorded with recovery options.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define permitted runbook actions, approvals, rollback procedures, and execution records before enabling agent-assisted production remediation.

questions.title: Culture: Has the team standardized shared AI tooling, practices, and AI-DLC workflows?
questions.description: Assess shared AI tooling, team working agreements, onboarding, version-controlled workflow rules, and controlled updates.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Maintain version-controlled workflow rules

helpfulResource.displayText: Teams use an approved workflow baseline with named owners and a reviewable change history.

improvementPlan.displayText: Publish the approved rules in version control and establish ownership, review, and distribution procedures.

choices.title: Define task-specific workflow tailoring criteria

helpfulResource.displayText: Workflow depth reflects task complexity and risk, with reasons recorded for omitting otherwise relevant activities.

improvementPlan.displayText: Document tailoring criteria for features, fixes, modernization, and other task types while retaining required controls.

choices.title: Validate workflow updates before wider adoption

helpfulResource.displayText: Changes to workflow rules are trialed on representative tasks and reviewed for unwanted effects.

improvementPlan.displayText: Pilot rule changes, compare results against acceptance expectations, and approve rollout with a rollback path.

choices.title: Standardize shared AI tooling and configurations

helpfulResource.displayText: The team maintains an approved shared toolset or supported tool profiles with common configuration, ownership, and access arrangements.

improvementPlan.displayText: Agree on supported AI tooling and shared configuration profiles and publish setup instructions, ownership, and change procedures.

choices.title: Reinforce shared AI practices through team enablement

helpfulResource.displayText: Working agreements, onboarding material, and practical learning sessions help team members use approved AI workflows consistently.

improvementPlan.displayText: Publish shared AI working agreements and onboarding material, run practical sessions, and use feedback to close adoption gaps.

questions.title: How do you apply organizational engineering standards to AI-generated work?
questions.description: Assess actionable engineering instructions, automated enforcement, and governed exceptions.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Provide approved engineering standards as agent context

helpfulResource.displayText: Current coding, architecture, security, and dependency requirements are available in maintained instructions or steering files.

improvementPlan.displayText: Translate applicable standards into actionable guidance, assign owners, and supply the approved version to development agents.

choices.title: Enforce machine-checkable standards in pipelines

helpfulResource.displayText: Automated checks verify applicable standards rather than relying solely on whether an agent follows written instructions.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement linting, dependency checks, security scans, and policy checks. Block changes that violate mandatory rules.

choices.title: Govern exceptions to organizational standards

helpfulResource.displayText: Approved exceptions identify an owner, rationale, scope, compensating controls, and a review or expiry date.

improvementPlan.displayText: Create an exception process and link each exception to affected artifacts and the authority that accepted the risk.

questions.title: How do you maintain consistent artifacts and completion criteria?
questions.description: Assess shared artifact structures, exit criteria, and operational readiness for each delivery increment.

helpfulResource.displayText: Reference basis: AWS guidance. Question wording and criticality are proposed custom-lens recommendations. Select every implemented practice supported by evidence.

choices.title: Use consistent templates for required artifacts

helpfulResource.displayText: Requirements, designs, decisions, and test reports follow shared structures that make required information easy to locate.

improvementPlan.displayText: Publish lightweight templates for required artifacts and tailor optional sections to the task s scope.

choices.title: Define explicit completion and phase exit criteria

helpfulResource.displayText: Work is considered complete only when applicable evidence and required reviews satisfy the stated criteria.

improvementPlan.displayText: Specify required artifacts, verification results, and approval responsibilities for each relevant completion checkpoint.

choices.title: Standardize operational readiness and handoff

helpfulResource.displayText: A production release has appropriate ownership, monitoring, runbooks, rollback procedures, and validated deployment configuration.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use a shared readiness checklist and resolve missing monitoring, recovery, documentation, or ownership before production handoff.

questions.title: Code: Is AI-assisted development a standard team practice or an individual choice?
questions.description: Assess the team s declared adoption model, routine use of approved AI assistance, and consistent handling of exceptions. Standard adoption does not require AI use for every change.

helpfulResource.displayText: Custom assessment practices added to cover the requested team-adoption topics. The reference supports related AI-DLC principles. It does not prescribe every practice below. Select all implemented practices supported by evidence. Document justified non-applicability where a capability is outside the team s scope.

choices.title: Define a team-wide AI-assisted development policy

helpfulResource.displayText: A documented team policy identifies expected AI-assisted activities, approved tools, and situations where individual discretion or an exception is appropriate.

improvementPlan.displayText: Agree on and publish the team adoption model, distinguishing routine expected use from optional use and justified exclusions.

choices.title: Embed approved AI assistance in the coding workflow

helpfulResource.displayText: Team working agreements and repository instructions describe how developers use AI for suitable implementation and refactoring work, with normal review and verification controls.

improvementPlan.displayText: Add approved AI-assisted coding steps to the shared workflow and provide examples for common implementation and refactoring tasks.

choices.title: Review adoption coverage and justified exceptions

helpfulResource.displayText: The team reviews whether agreed practices are used across relevant work and addresses access, training, or suitability issues. Evidence is based on work artifacts rather than individual surveillance.

improvementPlan.displayText: Periodically sample relevant work, record adoption barriers and justified exceptions, and update enablement or working agreements.
